african_elephant.in_the_wild: Savannas and forests of sub-Saharan Africa.
african_elephant.caveats: Many zoos keep only Asian elephants; those are recorded as related (Elephas maximus). Auckland and Phoenix Asian elephants excluded (moved / not on view).

lion.in_the_wild: Grasslands and savannas of sub-Saharan Africa; a small Asiatic population in Gir Forest, India.
lion.caveats: Asiatic lions (Panthera leo persica) at several UK/IE/FR zoos count as exact (same species).

cheetah.in_the_wild: Open savannas of eastern and southern Africa; a tiny remnant in Iran.
cheetah.caveats: Smithsonian National Zoo cheetah page says not currently on exhibit, so it is excluded.

leopard.in_the_wild: Forests, savannas and mountains across Africa and southern Asia.
leopard.caveats: Amur, Persian, Sri Lankan and Javan leopards count as exact. Snow leopard recorded as related (same genus); clouded leopard not used.

giraffe.in_the_wild: Savannas and open woodland of eastern and southern Africa.
giraffe.caveats: Giraffe taxonomy is in flux (1 vs 4 species); species_seen keeps the name the zoo uses.

zebra.in_the_wild: Grasslands of eastern and southern Africa (plains, Grevy's and mountain zebras).
zebra.caveats: Generic entry: plains, Grevy's and Hartmann's mountain zebra all count.

hippopotamus.in_the_wild: Rivers and lakes of sub-Saharan Africa.
hippopotamus.caveats: Pygmy hippo = related. Seed said Toronto has pygmy hippos only, but Toronto's Africa page (2026-09-30) lists River hippopotamus as viewable, so Toronto is exact. Whipsnade no longer has common hippos (pygmy only).

rhinoceros.in_the_wild: Savannas of Africa (white, black) and grasslands/forests of India, Nepal and Indonesia.
rhinoceros.caveats: Generic entry: any rhino species counts; species listed per place.

african_buffalo.in_the_wild: Savannas (Cape buffalo) and central/west African rainforests (forest buffalo).
african_buffalo.caveats: Rare in US zoos; most holdings are forest/Congo buffalo (Syncerus caffer nanus) in Europe. Asian water buffalo not used as related.

hyena.in_the_wild: Savannas and dry lands of Africa; striped hyena also in the Middle East and India.
hyena.caveats: Generic: spotted and striped hyena both count. Toronto hyena excluded (page says temporarily not viewable).

warthog.in_the_wild: Savannas and grasslands of sub-Saharan Africa.
warthog.caveats: Red river hog recorded as related (same family Suidae) where no warthog is listed.

meerkat.in_the_wild: Kalahari and Namib deserts and dry grasslands of southern Africa.
meerkat.caveats: German "Meerkatze" (a monkey) was deliberately excluded from keyword matching.

ostrich.caveats: Phoenix Zoo ostrich page says not currently on view; excluded.

baboon.in_the_wild: Savannas, hills and woodland across Africa and the southwest Arabian Peninsula.
baboon.caveats: Generic: hamadryas, olive, Guinea baboons count. Gelada = related. Spanish "papión" pages do not name the species.

gorilla.in_the_wild: Rainforests of central and west Africa.
gorilla.caveats: Nearly all captive gorillas are western lowland; Memphis lists Grauer's gorilla.

chimpanzee.in_the_wild: Rainforests and woodland savannas of west and central Africa.
chimpanzee.caveats: Bonobo recorded as related (same genus Pan).

african_wild_dog.in_the_wild: Savannas and open woodland of southern and eastern Africa.
african_wild_dog.caveats: Also called African painted dog or lycaon.

serval.in_the_wild: Wetlands and grasslands of sub-Saharan Africa.
serval.caveats: Often kept in small-cat or ambassador collections; fewer big-zoo profile pages.

method_notes: In practice this ran institution-centric within a species-centric batch: for ~120 candidate zoo domains I pulled robots.txt/sitemap.xml (~580 sitemap files), keyword-filtered URLs for the 18 animals plus German/French/Spanish names, then fetched every candidate page (~820) to confirm HTTP 200, a species title and a scientific name, and regex-flagged departure text ('not currently on view', 'has moved', 'temporarily not viewable'); flagged pages were read by hand. Zoos without sitemaps were covered by probing slug patterns (/animals/<common-name>, ~3,200 mostly-404 requests), and 6 JS-rendered or bot-blocked sites (Longleat, West Midlands Safari Park, Toronto, Bronx, AZA list, ZAA list) through a real browser. Search-snippet-only evidence (Dallas, San Diego Safari Park buffalo, Barcelona buffalo, Omaha/Fort Worth gorillas) is marked MED. Coordinates and images come from Wikidata P625/P18 (Q-ids recorded) and licences from the Commons API; OSM was used for CERZA and The Wilds (no clean Wikidata hit). Images were set to null where P18 shows an animal the place no longer holds (Zoo Atlanta panda, Twycross elephant) or the licence metadata was blank (Maryland). Accreditation: AZA list (Sept 2026) read via browser (403 to scripts); EAZA via the member JSON behind eaza.net/membership (covers UK/IE too, because the BIAZA member list is login-only); CAZA page; ZAA 'Find' page (its linked Locate page 404s, and South Australia is missing from it, so Adelaide Zoo and Monarto are 'unverified'). Howletts is an EAZA Temporary member. Blocked/slow: Wikidata search throttled (HTTP 429) and needed retries; Fort Wayne timed out (only 3 pre-fetched pages kept); Zoo Barcelona dropped script connections; Kansas City, Zoo Miami, Riverbanks, Busch Gardens and Disney's Animal Kingdom have no per-species pages we could reach, so they are absent. Wellington/Orana/Hamilton (NZ) were blocked or 404. Known risk: a species page existing does not prove the animal is on show today. Pages that say otherwise were excluded, but stale pages that say nothing can slip through. Toronto-style 'Viewable' flags are the gold standard. Scaling to ~600 institutions: build the institution list from accreditor lists first; run the sitemap+verify pipeline for all of them in one batch (it handles about 70% of zoos in minutes, and each zoo's crawl serves every species at once); use browser rendering only for the ~15% JS/bot-blocked sites; keep a per-domain slug-pattern table for probing; cache Wikidata by Q-id and throttle to 1 req/s; then do a human spot-check of about 5% of rows plus every MED row. Species-by-species web searching does not scale; institution crawling does.
